title: Prime-degree towers from the Galois p-property
statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic either $0$ or $p$. Assume that every finite Galois extension $N/F$ has degree a power of $p$. Galois means normal and separable: every irreducible polynomial over $F$ with a root in $N$ splits in $N$, and minimal polynomials of elements have distinct roots. For every finite field extension $L/F$ there are $n\ge0$ and intermediate fields $$F=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_n=L,\qquad [F_{i+1}:F_i]=p\quad(0\le i<n).$$ Degrees mean vector-space dimensions. No separability hypothesis is imposed on $L/F$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49, subgroup-chain argument and the separate purely inseparable argument; also proof of Corollary 6.1.6, printed p. 41.

proof.text: Every element of the finite-dimensional extension $L/F$ is algebraic: its powers are linearly dependent over $F$. Apply the separable-first lemma to obtain $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ with $E/F$ separable and $L/E$ purely inseparable. Both extensions are finite: $E$ is an $F$-linear subspace of $L$, and any finite $F$-spanning set of $L$ also spans over $E$. In characteristic zero the same lemma gives $E=L$.

source.place: Tag 030K, lemma-separable-first, including its characteristic-zero case.

proof.text: Apply the finite-Galois-envelope lemma to the single finite separable extension $E/F$. It gives an $F$-embedding $\iota:E\hookrightarrow N$ with $N/F$ finite Galois. Identify $E$ with its image for the subgroup argument. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$. The finite-Galois fixed-field theorem gives that $G$ is finite, $|G|=[N:F]$, and $N^G=F$. By the hypothesis of this item choose $a\geq0$ with $|G|=p^a$.

Let $H=\{g\in G:g|_E=1\}$. The Galois fixed-field recovery theorem for intermediate fields, applied to the Galois extension $N/F$ and its intermediate field $E$, gives $N^H=E$. The subgroup $H$ is finite and acts faithfully on $N$, so the finite-faithful-action theorem gives $[N:E]=|H|$. The intermediate fields are finite over $F$ as subspaces of $N$, and $N$ is finite over each because an $F$-spanning set still spans. Degree multiplicativity now gives $p^a=|H|[E:F]$. Unique factorization of positive integers implies $|H|=p^b$ for some $0\leq b\leq a$: every prime divisor of the positive divisor $|H|$ of $p^a$ must be $p$.

Construct $H_0,\ldots,H_{a-b}$ inductively with $H_0=H$, $H_j\subseteq H_{j+1}$, and $|H_j|=p^{b+j}$. At $j<a-b$, the integer $p^{b+j+1}$ divides $p^a=|G|$, so apply the subgroup-enlargement leaf to $H_j$. This supplies the next subgroup with the required containment and cardinality. At the last stage $H_{a-b}=G$, because it is a subset of the finite set $G$ with the same cardinality. If $a=b$ this is the length-zero chain.

source.place: The finite-group input to Tag 09DW, theorem-galois-theory: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_succ, Mathlib/GroupTheory/Sylow.lean:645-647; elementary finite induction.

proof.text: Set $r=a-b$ and $T_i=N^{H_{r-i}}$ for $0\leq i\leq r$. The defining fixed-point conditions give $T_i\subseteq T_{i+1}$; the endpoints are $T_0=F$ and $T_r=E$ by steps 2 and 3. Each subgroup acts faithfully, so the finite-action degree theorem gives $[N:T_i]=|H_{r-i}|=p^{a-i}$. For $i<r$, degree multiplicativity yields $p^{a-i}=p^{a-i-1}[T_{i+1}:T_i]$, hence $[T_{i+1}:T_i]=p$. These inclusions are strict because $p>1$. Pull this chain back through $\iota$: the inverse images of the $T_i\subseteq\iota(E)$ are intermediate fields of the original $E/F$, and $\iota$ maps a basis of each successive extension bijectively to a basis, so all successive degrees remain $p$.

source.place: Tags 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field) and 09G9 (lemma-multiplicativity-degrees); fixed-field inclusion follows directly from the definition.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}F=0$, then $E=L$, and the preceding chain finishes the proof. If $\operatorname{char}F=p$, the field $E$ also has characteristic $p$, since its structural inclusion is injective. Apply the purely-inseparable pth-root-tower theorem to the finite purely inseparable extension $L/E$: it gives $E=U_0\subset\cdots\subset U_s=L$ with each successive degree $p$. Concatenate the chain from $F$ to $E$ with this one, listing $E$ only once. Their finitely many intermediate fields lie in $L$ and every successive degree is $p$. Empty chains are allowed when either extension is trivial; in particular $L=F$ gives $n=0$.
